clue.text: High-ranking official with money meeting endless resentment

parts.note: brass is British slang for money

indicators.note: endless says the word for resentment loses its final letter

parts.note: resentment is hate

explanation.surface: A senior official is rich but bitterly resented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the last letter from HATE, leaving HAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass hat is slang for a senior military officer, so it is a high-ranking official.

clue.text: Bring back tree, to be transplanted with care

indicators.note: transplanted means moved about, so the letters are replanted in a new order

explanation.surface: A tree is to be moved to a new spot, carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be transplanted' rearranges TREE and CARE together.
explanation.definitionFit: To recreate something is to make it again, restoring what has gone.

clue.text: Under the sun disintegrate and fester

indicators.note: in a down answer, under places the second piece below the first

parts.note: to moulder is to decay away

explanation.surface: Something left out in the sun rots away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under' works because this is a down clue: MOULDER is written below S.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoulder, like fester, means to burn on slowly beneath the surface, used of resentment.

clue.text: Don't interfere with employees leaving work!

parts.note: workers are hands, as in farm hands
a worker who has left is off duty

explanation.surface: A warning to keep out of the way as the staff clock off.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an order to keep away and not meddle.

clue.text: Teacher gets nerd silly children's story

indicators.note: silly suggests the words are knocked into a foolish new order

explanation.surface: A teacher thinks a nerdy child is being foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges TEACHER GETS NERD, all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Frances Hodgson Burnett's novel of 1911 is a classic of children's fiction.

clue.text: Unruly seadog in. Californian port

indicators.note: an unruly crowd is out of order, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A rowdy old sailor is in town in a Californian harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unruly' rearranges SEADOG and IN together.
explanation.definitionFit: San Diego is a major Pacific harbour city in southern California.

clue.text: Some French bed with English style

parts.note: des is French for some
a crib is a child's bed

explanation.surface: A French bed in an English style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'style' is the verb: to style someone something is to call them that.
explanation.definitionFit: To describe someone as a thing is to call or label them, which is what styling them means.

clue.text: Frame a man deemed to have betrayed England

definitions.meaning: a window frame hinged at one side

definitions.text: a man deemed to have betrayed England
definitions.meaning: Sir Roger ... was hanged for treason in 1916 for seeking German help for an Irish rising

explanation.surface: A man is set up and branded a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frame' looks like a verb, 'to set up', but it is the noun: a hinged window.
explanation.definitionFit: A casement is a hinged window or its frame; Casement the Irish nationalist was executed as a traitor to the British Crown.

clue.text: Dance goddess hanging around a bar

indicators.note: the goddess's name hangs around the other pieces, holding them inside it

parts.note: Hera is the Greek queen of the gods
to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: A goddess is seen loitering near a pub's bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging around' is the container signal: the goddess's name wraps the other two pieces, so 'bar' is the verb to ban, not a pub counter.
explanation.definitionFit: The habanera is a slow Cuban dance in duple time, made famous by an aria in the opera Carmen.

clue.text: Try to get hold of gun possibly, wanting score settled outside

indicators.note: outside says one rearranged word goes around the other
settled means the letters of score are rearranged, put in a new order
possibly says gun is only one way to arrange these letters

explanation.surface: Someone after a gun wants an old score settled first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns GUN into UNG; 'settled' turns SCORE into SCRO...E, which goes 'outside' UNG.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrounge is to try to get something for free by cadging or begging.

clue.text: Member of sect is unhappy, you understand from conversation

parts.note: unhappy means sad

indicators.note: from conversation says the words are taken as they are spoken, not spelt

parts.note: spoken casually, 'you understand?' is the tag 'd'you see?'

explanation.surface: A sect member is downcast, as you'll gather from talking to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from conversation' tells you to say 'd'you see' aloud, which sounds like DUCEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sadducees were a Jewish religious party in the time of Jesus, rivals of the Pharisees.

clue.text: City girl in lowest social categories, put down the social ladder

indicators.note: in says the city and girl pieces sit inside the social categories

parts.note: D and E are the two lowest grades in the British socio-economic classification
EC is the postcode for the City of London
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl from the City ends up among the poorest classes, losing status.
explanation.walkthrough: In British market research, people are graded A, B, C1, C2, D and E, so the lowest two give D...E.
explanation.definitionFit: Déclassé means having fallen in social standing, so it describes someone moved down the social ladder.

clue.text: All together, holding firm, the man is about to gain victory

annotationWithheld.why: All together, holding firm, the man is about to gain victory (8): CO (firm) + HE'S (the man is) leaves IVE, which 'about to gain victory' does not clearly give; no source found
annotationWithheld.clue: All together, holding firm, the man is about to gain victory

clue.text: National park terrified female gets round with others in pursuit

parts.note: petrified means terrified
O is round in shape
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A frightened woman runs off, with others chasing her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in pursuit' just places REST behind the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrified Forest is a US national park in Arizona, known for its fossilised trees.

clue.text: Ascribe later day to mail that has arrived on time

indicators.note: the mail has turned up ahead of the time, so it comes first

parts.note: post means mail
a date is a point in time

explanation.surface: Putting a later date on a letter that arrived punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: To postdate a cheque or letter is to write a date on it later than the true one.

clue.text: Government department's attempt to conceal a ruse that's failed

indicators.note: to conceal says the attempt word hides the next piece inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: a failed ruse falls apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ministry tries to cover up a scheme that went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's failed' rearranges A RUSE into EASUR, which TRY conceals; the 's after 'department' stands for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Treasury is the UK finance ministry, in charge of public money.

clue.text: Actually present at home, a junior member of the family

parts.note: in means at home
per means a, as in once per day
a son is a younger member of a family

explanation.surface: A young family member is there at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' gives PER, as in so much per head.
explanation.definitionFit: To be somewhere in person is to be physically there yourself.

clue.text: Something potentially dangerous in mines aroused a politician

parts.note: fired up means aroused
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician got stirred up about mine safety.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedamp is methane gas that can explode in coal mines.

clue.text: Hand' offered in authentic action to cancel obligation?

indicators.note: offered in says the hand is placed inside the authentic word

parts.note: real means authentic
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: A hand held out in a genuine gesture to let someone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offered in' is the container signal. The question mark warns that the definition describes the word loosely, by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A remittal is an act of remitting, letting someone off a debt or penalty.

clue.text: Gaoler is relocated in sultan's palace

indicators.note: relocated means moved somewhere else, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: A jailer is transferred to a sultan's palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is relocated' rearranges GAOLER and IS together.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the women's quarters of a Muslim palace, and so the sultan's palace itself.

clue.text: Comprehensive work for Mrs Mopp

definitions.meaning: a ... change is wide-ranging, covering everything
Mrs Mopp was the charlady in the British radio comedy ITMA; cleaning floors was her job

explanation.surface: A cleaner's job is all-embracing.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Mopp, from the wartime BBC radio show ITMA, became a byword for a British cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweeping review is broad and thorough; brushing floors is a cleaner's chore.

clue.text: Member of New World community, a fellow fine inside

annotationWithheld.why: Member of New World community, a fellow fine inside (8): A MAN round ERIC would give it, but 'fine' does not give ERIC; scan confirms the wording
annotationWithheld.clue: Member of New World community, a fellow fine inside

clue.text: Old warhorse offers series of shocks tossing rider around

indicators.note: around says the shuffled rider goes round the shocks
tossing means the letters of rider are thrown into a new order

parts.note: EST is short for electroshock therapy, a course of electric shocks

explanation.surface: An old warhorse throws its rider off after a series of jolts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossing' rearranges the rider's letters, and 'around' puts them round the shocks. EST, electroshock therapy, is chiefly an American abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A destrier was a medieval knight's charger, the horse ridden into battle.

clue.text: Little lady with a long scarf is a bit of a heart-throb

parts.note: Di is a short form of the name Diana
a stole is a long scarf worn over the shoulders

explanation.surface: A small woman in a long wrap is quite a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart-throb' looks like a pin-up, but read literally it is one beat of the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Diastole is the phase of each heartbeat when the heart relaxes and fills, so it is part of one throb.

clue.text: Reptile seen in wrong part of France

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
the Oise is a French department north of Paris

explanation.surface: A reptile is spotted in the wrong region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortoise is a slow land-dwelling reptile with a shell.

clue.text: A European captured by none — except the English!

definitions.text: A European captured by none — except the English!

indicators.note: captured by says the first pieces are held inside the next
except the English says the letter E, for English, is dropped from none

parts.note: taken as written
a Pole is a European

explanation.surface: A European was beaten by nobody, except the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except the English' drops E, leaving NON, and 'captured by' puts the pieces inside it. The whole clue is the definition too: the English captured the French emperor after Waterloo.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte was a European ruler finally defeated and taken prisoner by the British.
